In the matter of :
Master Shivram (Injured)

The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of FIR No.201/2017 Police Station Ghazipur, Delhi.
2. Briefly stated the facts of the present case as mentioned in the FIR are that during emergency duty, a call was received that a child has been run over by a truck and when police official visited the spot, the caller and eye witness could not be met and thereafter, it was learnt that another DD call was received regarding quarrel and on reaching at the spot, it was learnt that the child had been taken to LBS hospital but thereafter, as no treatment was given, he was taken back home and thereafter child was again taken to LBS Hospital for treatment by PCR and on visiting police station,
the child was found not fit for statement and an FIR was registered on the basis of MLC and condition of child u/s 279/338 IPC.

In the charge- sheet, it is mentioned that during investigation,
Shivram vs Mukesh Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99083508/
1 eye witness i.e. father of the injured child was met and disclosed the number of offending truck as RJ- 02GA-7981 and the offending vehicle was produced by the registered owner.

After investigation,
charge-sheet was filed against the driver and offending truck / R-1 and final opinion of the MLC of the child was given as grievous.
During investigation, it was found that the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent No.1 and owned by respondent No.2.

In connection with the accident,
an FIR bearing No. 201/17 was registered at the police station Gazipur, Delhi.
3. Respondent no. 1 & 2 have appeared before the Tribunal and filed their separate replies.
Insurance company / R-3 also filed reply.
3.1 R-1 has mentioned in the written statement that the alleged incident had not occurred and his vehicle is falsely implicated in collision with police.
The alleged vehicle was duly insured.

3.2 R-2 has filed his reply on the similar lines and stated that his vehicle has been falsely roped in the FIR in connivance with police and his vehicle as duly insured and R-1 had a valid driving licence.
The certificate of fitness and all other documents were provided to IO during investigation.

4. The respondent no. 3 insurance company / United India Assurance Company Ltd filed its separate written statement and has taken the general defences and also stated that as per the MLC,
the injury was not sustained from any accident caused by a motor vehicle and 'fall from stairs' has been mentioned in MLC.
The insurance policy was valid on the date of alleged accident.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 07.12.2017:-
(i) Whether Master Shivram aged about 12 years suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular on 15.07.2017 at about 6:30 pm near DJB office, Sulabh Sauchalya, Gali No.
7, Gazipur Dairy farm, Delhi, within jurisdciton PS Gazipur, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving motor vehicle bearing registration No. RJ-02-GA-7981 (HGV)
driven by R-1 / Mukesh Kumar?
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
(iii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate and for which period?OPP
(iv) Relief.
6. In order to establish the claim of minor injured / petitioner, one witness was examined.

6.1 PW1 / father of the minor petitioner Biltoo Mukhia has entered into witness box and deposed on an affidavit Ex. PW1/1 about the manner of the accident, rash and negligent driving by R-1, injuries suffered by the minor petitioner and expenses incurred on the treatment of the petitioner.

The following documents were relied upon by him in his evidence :-

PW1/B  DAR is Ex. PW1/C 6.3
Respondent No.3 chose to lead evidence in defence and examined one witness as R3W1.
R3W1 Dr. Virendra, Medical officer, LBS Hospital, deposed that the MLC of petitioner Shivram was prepared under his supervision.
He also deposed that he could not comment on the medical history of petitioner as mentioned in emergency slip Ex. PW1/B.

He also deposed that the said document was not shown to the doctor at the time of preparing the MLC and further that in the column of alleged history of patient, RTA (Road Traffic Accident) is mentioned.
7. Respondents No.1 and 2 did not led any evidence in support of their defence.

8. I have heard Sh. Rahul Thakur, counsel for petitioner and Sh.
G.D. Sharma, Ld. Counsel for R-3 / insurer.
None has come forward to address arguments on behalf of respondents No.1 and 2.
I have also perused the record.

9. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE NO. 1.
10.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.

Reliance is placed in cases titled as Sunita & Ors. vs.
Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2020) 13 SCC 486 and Kusum Lata & Ors. Vs.
Satbir & Ors. (2011) 3 SCC 646.
11.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, PW-1 / father of the petitioner has been examined and has proved that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.1.

PW1 has deposed that on 15.07.2017 at about 6:30 pm, his son / minor petitioner Shivram was standing on road side near park and at the same time, the offending vehicle bearing No.RJ-02GA-7981 (HGV) being driven by R-1 at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from back side and hit the petitioner child with a violent force, resulting in multiple grievous injuries to him and he was immediately admitted in LBS Hospital.
Insurance company has relied on the document Ex. PW1/B to assail the claim of the petitioner but I find no merit in the contention raised by the insurance company.
It is noteworthy to mention that copy of DD No. 31A dated 15.07.2017, PS Gazipur shows that at 7:35 pm (19:35 hours), it was reported that near Gazipur Jal Board, one child was run over by a truck.
It is also mentioned in the DD that on receiving the intimation, when ASI Bijender reached at the spot, no one was found and the number of the caller could not be connected.

Further, at about 11:00 am, SI Neeraj informed that he had received another DD No. 33A at 10:42 pm (22:42 hours)
to the effect that there was quarrel at Gali No. 7 Ghaizpur dairy farm and on reaching there, it was Shivram vs Mukesh Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99083508/
3 learnt that victim child, (pursuant to the injuries sustained in the accident), had been taken to LBS Hospital but as no treatment was given, he had been brought home and thereafter, PCR Van had taken the child to LBS Hospital.
The child was found unfit for statement and hospital was visited and FIR was registered on the basis of MLC and condition of the child.

From perusal of the charge-sheet as well as the document on record, it can be fairly concluded that pursuant to the accident and sustaining of injuries by the child, call was made to the police after the accident and thereafter, a call regarding quarrel was also received subsequently, which only indicates that there was some quarrel pursuant to the road accident in question.
Nothing has been brought to suggest that any history of injuries sustained in any quarrel was given to the police either by injured or his father or any other eye witness.
PW1 clearly deposed in his cross-examination that he was present at the time of accident and offending vehicle had hit his child from front side.
He also deposed that he had made call to the police at 100 number and informed about the accident.
He denied that the his son had fallen from stairs.
From DD No.31A in question, it is clear that an accident was reported to the police and no information was given regarding the presence of the injured at home fall from the stairs.

Merely because on one of the paper prepared at LBS Hospital, 'history of fall from stairs' is mentioned, no bizarre conclusion can be made by the Tribunal that the injuries were sustained due to fall from stairs, when neither the charge-sheet nor MLC or testimony of the eye witness reflect so.
It is further observed that on the same document Ex.PW1/B on the same date, it is also observed by the same doctor on the backside that alleged history of fall while playing was reported.

The doctor concerned was not examined to throw light on as to who had given the alleged history and why two different alleged history was given on the same document prepared on the same day and it can be seen as nothing but an oversight by the doctor concerned and either a human error or history not properly given to doctor by someone not aware regarding the factum of accident.
PW1 was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for R-3 and his testimony remained intact.

Even, respondents No.1 and 2 have not led any evidence to diminish the claim of the petitioner and it is not the defence taken by the insurance company that R-1 and R-2 are in connivance with the petitioner.
No such suggestion was given to PW1 by Ld. Counsel for R-3 / insurer.

Hence, it stands proved that the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata truck (HGV open body) by the respondent no. 1.
12.
After investigation, police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1/ the driver of the Tata truck.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
( New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima-facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

If the Tribunal feels that charge- sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.

,
did not lead any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

sentences.text: Even the insurance company has not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.
15. Further, it is not disputed that respondent No.1 was charge-sheeted in the aforesaid criminal case for causing the accident by driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
It is also seen that R-1 was also charge-sheeted for driving the vehicle without valid driving licence.
However, on the basis of DAR and charge-sheet filed by IO and medical documents, it can be concluded that grievous injuries were sustained by the petitioner due to the accident in question.
Thus, prima- facie, it is clear that respondent No.1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner at the time of accident.

16. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, and for filing of charge-sheet and testimonies on record, it is proved that the petitioner Shivram received grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Mukesh Kumar, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

ISSUE No.2 17. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

18. The present claim petition pertains to injury and scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and Shivram vs Mukesh Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99083508/
5 mental stress in life."
19. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
5.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

6. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
 (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage)
 (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of  normal longevity).
Shivram vs Mukesh Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99083508/
6
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses,
loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
20.
Now, in the present case, the injured Shivram had suffered from grievous injury.
Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows -

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
21.
Under this head, actual medical bills are reimbursed.
No original medical bill has been proved on record.
Therefore, no amount is being given as compensation under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME (DURING TREATMENT):
22.
It is not disputed that petitioner was 12 years old at the time of accident and it was stated that he was studying at that time.
Since petitioner was not working or earning, no loss of income can be considered.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
23.

PW1 has produced on record medical treatment record of the minor petitioner from LBS Hospital and GTB Hospital Ex.PW1/B, which reflect that he visited hospital for treatment at least till 22.07.2017 and further that petitioner suffered from fractures i.e.right superior pubic ramus and medial melleaous.
Further, MLC Ex. RW3/1 reflects that the final opinion on the nature of injuries was given as 'grievous'.

Hence, considering the nature of injuries and the treatment discussed above,
an inference can be drawn that the petitioner child must have suffered pain, shock, frustration and deprivation of ordinary pleasures including visit to school for a long time and therefore, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded to petitioner under this head.

CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
24.

Though no document has been produced to show the expenses under this head, however,
considering the nature of injuries and treatment provided to the petitioner, it may be safely assumed that the minor petitioner must have required the services of an adult person for his care in the hospital and even after his discharge till the time he had completely recovered.

Further, a reasonable amount must have been spent on the special diet needed for quick recovery after surgery and on transportation facility required for taking injured to hospital / doctors for the purpose of treatment.
Thus, a total sum of Rs.20,000/- is granted to petitioner towards conveyance and special diet.

25. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment, it cannot be ignored that family members of minor petitioner might have had to render Shivram vs Mukesh Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99083508/
7
their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- as attendant charges.
26. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.30,000/- (20,000+10,000) under this head.

27. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 Sl. No. Head of compensation Amount  1. Medical Expenses Nil.
 2. Pain & Suffering Rs.40,000/-
3 . Loss of Income during Nil.
treatment

4. Conveyance, attendant & Rs.30,000/-
 Special Diet Charges  TOTAL Rs.70,000/-
 (rounded off  Rs.70,000/-)
28.
Petitioner has been pursuing this case since the year 2017.

Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization (excluding the period of for which the interest had been waived by orders of the Tribunal).

As per record, vide order dated 02.04.2018, it was ordered that "since the case is not able to proceed on account of laxity on the part of the petitioner, he will not be entitled to interest for the intervening period from the date of framing of issues till commencement of his evidence.
The issues were framed on 07.12.2017 whereas the evidence commenced only on 19.11.2018.
Accordingly, due to default on the part of the petitioner, the petitioner would not be entitled for interest from 07.12.2017 till 19.11.2018 on the award amount.

LIABILITY:
29.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents are liable to pay the compensation amount.

As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and, in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.3/ insurance company namely United India Insurance Co. Ltd becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
RELIEF:

Shivram vs Mukesh Kumar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99083508/
8 30.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.70,000/- (rupees seventy thousand only) along with interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization (excluding the period from 07.12.2017 till 19.11.2018) in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3 / United India Assurance Company Ltd.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
